 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. The Toronto Raptors are looking to end a four-game losing streak tonight as they face the reigning champion New York Knicks for the second time in three days. Despite the disheartening results over the past week, the Raptors have had their chances, holding double-digit leads in each of their last three games. Trying to maintain offensive consistency with both Kawhi Leonard and Scottie Barnes out proved to be extremely difficult, but even with Barnes back against New York, he needed help down the stretch.
 Tonight marks a new opportunity, though. In the grand scheme of things, these games are just chances for the role players to prove their worth next to Barnes in the clutch. Leonard will be there to save the day at some point, but right now it's on head coach Darko Rajakovic and his team to figure out how to hold leads and play their best basketball in the most important moments.
 Toronto Raptors forward Scottie Barnes (4) | Kevin Sousa-Kevin Sousa-Imagn Images
 Heading into tonight's matchup, there are no surprises on the injury report . Leonard is again ruled out, but the Raptors provided an update on his recovery, citing progress; he will be reevaluated in another week. He is joined on the sidelines by the three two-way players, Nate Bittle, Malachi Smith, and Kevin McCullar Jr. Barnes was initially listed as questionable due to an illness, but has been cleared to play. New York again boasts a completely clean sheet.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Keys for Revenge
 It's important for the Raptors to properly respond to Sunday's loss and not overreact. Ultimately, they did what they wanted to in most categories; they had more rebounds, assists, fastbreak points, and points in the paint, along with fewer turnovers. New York saw 100 of its 112 points come from just four players: Jalen Brunson, Karl-Anthony Towns, OG Anunoby, and Landry Shamet. Shamet's 23 points marked the eighth-highest-scoring game of his nine-year career ( via StatMuse ); the Raptors cannot put their focus on his explosive offense because the likelihood of it happening again is slim to none.
 Brunson, Towns, and Anunoby played over 40 minutes in the contest; the best way to make sure this doesn't happen again is to attack them constantly in the first quarter. Without Towns' 17 rebounds, the Raptors would dominate the paint, so if they can feed the ball to Jakob Poeltl and Collin Murray-Boyles down low, they'll have a great chance to put him in foul trouble early. The same goes for Brunson; if the Raptors can matchup hunt to get him to switch on to Barnes, he'll have no choice but to foul because he lacks the size or athleticism to stay with Barnes when he attacks the rim. If he is forced to go to the bench early, the Knicks will be scrambling to find an offensive rhythm early in the game, which is an easy spot for Toronto to take advantage of.
 New York Knicks guard Jalen Brunson (11) and Toronto Raptors forward Scottie Barnes (4) | Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images
 As far as keeping that advantage, it is going to come down to half-court offense without Barnes. The team needs consistent ball movement: screening both on and off the ball, cutting to the rim, and quick passes to get the defense out of rotation and create spacing and favorable matchups. Isolation offense from RJ Barrett and Immanuel Quickley has not worked very often over the last two years, so they need to finally put their foot down and go away from it if they want to avoid falling into a tie for 10th place in the Eastern Conference.
